newsitem.title: GERMANY: German decision on Eurofighter in summer - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: German decision on Eurofighter in summer - Waigel.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said the German government will make a final decision on financing the procurement of the Eurofighter combat jet when it drafts its 1998 budget this summer.
Waigel, in remarks carried on ARD public television on Monday night, restated Germany's commitment to backing the four-country aircraft project.
"Experts say that we urgently need such a fighter," Waigel said.
"If we need it, it should be built in Germany because we have already spent billions (of marks) on research and development and because we have clear agreements with several European countries."
Waigel added, however, that a final decision would not be made on the short- and medium-term financing of the project until June or July of this year.

Defence Minister Volker Ruehe had sought an earlier decision by Bonn to commit to buying 180 Eurofighters after he hammered out a total price of 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion) with German partner Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA).
But the cash-strapped government, struggling to meet borrowing targets to qualify for Europe's single currency, has put off a decision.
Britain and Spain have already made a commitment to buy their Eurofighters. The project's partners are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.
DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff said his company was spending a million marks a day to keep the Eurofighter project alive without having any firm promise from Germany to buy.
"There would be a European row if preparations for production were to stop tomorrow," Bischoff told ARD.

Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier, finance spokeswoman of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said her party did not support the Eurofighter project and state funds could be better channelled into civil aviation projects.
